toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: Collected two items. X8 splits the FCR fall by contact reason, referral status and tenure. X1 is the Finance change record, which gives the mechanism. I also compared the date of each April change with the weekly FCR series and checked that X8's figures reconcile to the site averages.
output.brief:
The fall is not mainly about the April starters, the tariff rise, the IVR or workload. On 14 April Finance cut the amount an agent can credit during a call from £100 to £25, after an audit finding. Anything bigger is now automatically referred to Billing Resolution. The share of billing calls referred jumped from 7% to 54% that week. Referred calls are resolved first time only about a third of the time (82% otherwise), largely because customers ring back to chase. That alone reproduces the whole drop. Tenured agents fell as far as the new starters, who are under a point lower; tariff calls resolve at 85%; the drop was complete before the IVR changed. Customer Operations wasn't consulted.

I'm about 90% sure of the cause; the link to complaints is only a coincidence in timing.

Next: drop the performance-plan proposal, which would penalise people for a rule change. Agree a revised in-call limit with Finance, backed by post-call sampling, and trial it on two teams for six weeks, tracking FCR and unsupported credits. Finance has said it would consider this. Use MI's one-day reruns for tracking rather than a three-month dashboard rebuild.
